note: Rewritten from Chhotani (Rec. Zool. Surv. India, Occasional Paper No. 171, Termite fauna of north-eastern India), original in English. Holotype data: Lake Ganga, Itanagar, Lower Subansiri Dist., Arunachal Pradesh, collected by O. B. Chhotani on 15 May 1989 (month 5, day 15) from "a piece of timber", one soldier and one worker in a single vial; alate unknown; the distribution also includes China (see Hsia and Fan 1968). Original pagination: text pp. 51—52 (page footer 52 visible).

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head narrower, sides nearly straight (head width 1.18 mm, width/length index 0.761), postmentum waist shorter; distinguished from R. chinensis and allied species by the head shape, the length of the postmentum waist and the fine, weak crenulations on the inner margin of the mandibles. Alate unknown.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow, antennae slightly paler, labrum transparent yellowish brown, mandibles reddish brown with red-yellow bases, legs and body milky white. Head and body densely hairy (head more sparsely so). Total body length 5.10 mm. Head oblong-oval, sides slightly convex, widest at the middle, slightly narrowed both anteriorly and posteriorly, posterior margin rounded. Frons inclined forward at an angle of 45 degrees; the middle of the frontal area concave, with a weak swelling on each side at the base. Fontanelle minute, situated at two-thirds of the head length from the posterior margin to the mandibular base. Compound eyes and ocelli absent. Antennae 16-segmented, segment 3 shortest, segment 4 slightly larger than segment 3, segment 5 slightly smaller than segment 4 but larger than segment 3, remaining segments pear-shaped. Postclypeus flat, narrow, indistinctly delimited from the frons, with one small hair on each side. Anteclypeus semitransparent, hairless, narrow, band-like. Labrum triangular, as long as wide, apex broadly rounded, with a pair of long hairs at the apex and several short hairs on the surface. Mandibles sword-shaped, apices slightly incurved; outer margin of the left mandible slightly incurved, that of the right mandible slightly convex; the basal half of the inner margin of the left mandible with very fine, weak crenulations. Postmentum rod-shaped, the waist strongly incurved. Pronotum flat, with a weak notch in the middle of the anterior margin, the anterior margin slightly raised in lateral view, posterior margin weakly concave. Mesonotum semicircular, narrower than the pronotum; metanotum slightly wider than the mesonotum and as wide as the pronotum, the posterior margins of both weakly convex. Legs short, hairy, tibial spur formula 3:2:2, tarsi 4-segmented. Abdomen elongate, with cerci and styli. Measurements (mm, holotype): total body length 5.10; head length (with mandibles) 2.40; head length (to mandibular base) 1.55; maximum head width 1.18; head width (at mandibular base) 0.90; head height 0.80; occiput–fontanelle distance (measured from the posterior margin of the head) 1.08; head index (width/head length to mandibular base) 0.761; head constriction index (width at mandibular base/maximum width) 0.763; occiput–fontanelle index 0.697; labrum length 0.28, width 0.25; mandible length: left 0.95, right 0.93; mandible–head length index (left mandible length/head length to mandibular base) 0.613; postmentum median length 1.00, maximum width 0.43, waist width 0.15; pronotum length 0.50, width 0.80.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head pale milky white, antennae, legs and body nearly white. Head and body densely hairy. Total body length 4.10 mm. Head capsule nearly circular, wider than the head length to the mandibular base (head length with labrum 1.15, head length to mandibular base 0.93, width 1.00 mm). Fontanelle indistinct. Compound eyes and ocelli absent. Postclypeus weakly convex, one quarter as long as wide (length 0.1, width 0.40 mm). Labrum wide, dome-shaped, with several hairs on the anterior part and on the surface (length 0.25, width 0.43 mm). Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 slightly shorter than segment 2.
